title: Scope the search
brief:
You are on the products page. Write a test that:

1. adds the **first** product to the cart
2. waits for the *Added!* pop-up to appear
3. opens the cart using the **View Cart** link **inside that pop-up**
4. checks the address is `https://automationexercise.com/view_cart`

Step 3 is the hard one, and it is hard for two reasons at once. Try the obvious thing first and read what Playwright tells you - both failures are worth meeting.

:::tip Remember
Name matching is a substring, and while the pop-up is open there is a *Cart* link in the menu **and** a *View Cart* link in the pop-up.
:::
starter:
from playwright.sync_api import Page, expect


def test_view_cart_from_the_added_popup(page: Page):
    page.goto("https://automationexercise.com/products")

    # 1. add the first product

    # 2. wait for the pop-up

    # 3. click View Cart INSIDE the pop-up

    # 4. check where you ended up
solution:
from playwright.sync_api import Page, expect


def test_view_cart_from_the_added_popup(page: Page):
    page.goto("https://automationexercise.com/products")

    page.get_by_role("link", name="Add to cart").first.click()

    modal = page.locator("#cartModal")
    expect(modal).to_be_visible()

    modal.get_by_role("link", name="Cart").click()

    expect(page).to_have_url("https://automationexercise.com/view_cart")

checks.label: Exactly one product is in the cart
checks.feedback: The cart does not hold exactly one product. There are eight 'Add to cart' links on this page, so an unqualified locator is a strict-mode violation - add .first.

checks.label: You scoped the Cart link to the pop-up
checks.feedback: You got to the cart, but not by scoping. If you used .last you relied on the pop-up being the last thing in the document - true today, and one layout change from being false. Say what you mean instead: page.locator("#cartModal").get_by_role("link", name="Cart").

checks.name: to_be_visible
checks.label: You wait for the pop-up before clicking into it
checks.feedback: No to_be_visible check ran. The pop-up takes 300 ms to appear; without that wait you are clicking at a moment that may or may not exist yet.

checks.label: You end up on the cart page

hints.label: Nudge
hints.text: Two separate problems. Adding: eight links say 'Add to cart', so pick one. Opening the cart: two links match name="Cart", and the one in the menu is underneath the pop-up's grey backdrop.

hints.label: Strategy
hints.text: Give the pop-up a name: modal = page.locator("#cartModal"). Wait for it with expect(modal).to_be_visible(). Then search INSIDE it: modal.get_by_role("link", name="Cart").click().

hints.label: Solution
hints.text: page.get_by_role("link", name="Add to cart").first.click(); modal = page.locator("#cartModal"); expect(modal).to_be_visible(); modal.get_by_role("link", name="Cart").click(); expect(page).to_have_url("https://automationexercise.com/view_cart")

reveal:
Two lessons in one challenge.

**Ambiguity is fixed by saying what you mean.** `.first` and `.last` work by position; scoping works by meaning. `pages/base_page.py` in the kit does exactly this, with a comment explaining the same trap:

```python
self.page.locator(".shop-menu").get_by_role("link", name="Cart").click()
```

**Playwright will not click through an overlay.** If you tried the menu link, you got `intercepts pointer events` rather than a click that silently went to the backdrop. A real user could not have clicked it either.
